title: Long-Tail Learning via Logit Adjustment
authors: Aditya Krishna Menon, Sadeep Jayasumana, Ankit Singh Rawat, Himanshu Jain, Andreas Veit, Sanjiv Kumar
conclusions: Proposes 'logit adjustment': adding a label-frequency-dependent offset (tau * log(pi_y)) to the logits, either post-hoc on a trained classifier (Eq. 9) or baked into the softmax cross-entropy loss during training (Eq. 10), to counter long-tail/class-imbalance bias.

Shows this is Fisher-consistent for minimizing the balanced error (average per-class error rate), unlike prior post-hoc weight-normalisation or margin-based loss-modification schemes (Cao et al. 2019 LDAM, Tan et al. 2020 equalised loss), which are proven inconsistent even in simple binary settings.

Unifies several prior proposals (balanced loss, LDAM adaptive margin, equalised margin) as special cases of a general pairwise-margin loss (Eq. 11), and gives a necessary/sufficient consistency condition (Theorem 1).

Empirically validates on CIFAR-10/100-LT, ImageNet-LT and iNaturalist: both post-hoc logit adjustment and the logit-adjusted loss reduce balanced error over ERM, weight normalisation, and margin-based losses, with the biggest gains on rare/tail classes (Fig. 4).

The method only ever reweights logits/decision thresholds based on fixed class priors; it optimizes population-level balanced error and gives no mechanism to guarantee or bound how many test instances actually get predicted into any given class.
our_use: Cited in a list of imbalance/cost-sensitive techniques the paper contrasts itself against: 'label-distribution-aware margins \citep{cao2019learning}, prior-corrected logits \citep{menon2021logit}. None of it guarantees the prediction count; the realized number of constrained-class predictions remains a free outcome. TraLO targets the count directly.' (final_AAAI_PAPER/main.tex, related-work paragraph around line 209-214).
issues: none — title, full author list (incl. spelling), and venue/year (ICLR 2021) all match the PDF front matter exactly. ICLR entries conventionally carry no volume/number/page range (OpenReview-hosted, non-paginated proceedings), so the absence of those fields is not an omission. The characterization as a 'prior-corrected logits' technique that adjusts decision boundaries via class-frequency offsets but does not constrain/guarantee the realized prediction count is an accurate description of the paper's method (Eqs. 8-10 explicitly operate on balanced-error-optimal logit offsets, not count constraints).
